findings.title: Team admin/owner check is AND and never matches a real role
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to both be true. Membership has a single role, so a team admin is not an owner and an owner is not an admin; the branch is dead for normal memberships. Team admins and owners therefore cannot add guests unless they are also booking.userId or an attendee. Collective co-hosts who are only on the event hosts/references (not booking.userId and not attendees) are rejected as well. The bookings UI treats admin and owner as alternatives (isUserTeamAdminOrOwner) and still shows the action, so those users get FORBIDDEN. The check needs to be OR, and other hosts on the booking need to be allowed.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the actor's credentials, not the host's
findings.body: The query loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar, but updateCalendarAttendees is called with an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar references store the host credential id. This handler explicitly allows attendees, and the booker is an attendee while booking.userId is the host, so the booker path — a primary use of "add guests" — does not have those credential ids. The host calendar event is then not updated (or the call throws). The same happens for a team admin acting on someone else's booking, and even the owner path only has one user's credentials, so other collective hosts' calendar references are skipped. Guests can be stored while the existing invites still list the old attendees.

findings.title: Attendees are committed before calendar and email, with no recovery
findings.body: prisma.booking.update createMany commits the new Attendee rows before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails. Only the email call is in try/catch, and that catch logs a fixed string, drops the error object, and then the handler still returns success. If the calendar update throws (wrong credentials, provider error), the mutation 500s after the rows exist, emails never run, and AddGuestsDialog does not invalidate the bookings query on error. A retry treats those addresses as already invited and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the guests stay on the booking with no mail and no calendar update, and the user cannot retry. There is no compensation or idempotent resend.

findings.title: Attendees can fan out meeting invites with no state or guest limits
findings.body: The only gate is organizer, attendee email match, or the broken team-admin check. booking.status and endTime are never read, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING, and already-ended bookings. The new mailers always attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED (attendee-add-guests-email.ts line 15, organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 19) and the payload includes the video URL from booking references, so a pending or cancelled meeting's join link is emailed as a confirmed invite. eventType.disableGuests is never read, so this bypasses the public booking form's no-guests setting. ZAddGuestsInputSchema.guests (addGuests.schema.ts line 5) is an unbounded email array, and each new address gets AttendeeScheduledEmail. Newly added guests are stored as attendees, so anyone with a Cal.com account for that address can invite more people. This is an authedProcedure, not limited to the bookings page.

findings.title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is bypassed by case and spaces
findings.body: The env list is lowercased but not trimmed, and the filter uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) on the raw input. Zod email() does not lowercase, so Banned@example.com is inserted and then mailed when the list contains banned@example.com. A space after a comma ("a@x.com, b@x.com") makes every entry after the first fail to match. Blacklisted addresses that do match are dropped silently; if any other address remains, the handler still returns success, so the client toasts that every submitted guest was added.

findings.title: Guest dedup is case-sensitive, racy, and not applied inside the request
findings.body: uniqueGuests only drops an address when guest === attendee.email against the pre-read attendee list. A@x.com versus a@x.com, the same address twice in one payload, and the organizer's own email are all inserted. Nothing in this path enforces uniqueness, and the check-then-act is not transactional, so two concurrent calls with the same new address both pass the filter and both create rows. Emails are stored with the original casing, so later exact-match checks keep missing them. When every address is filtered, the error is emails_must_be_unique_valid, which is wrong for "already on the booking".

findings.title: Notification uses the raw guest list, so existing attendees get a new booking email
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with guests, the original input, not uniqueGuests. In email-manager.ts, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a fresh confirmation plus an ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The dialog never receives the current attendee list, so submitting one already-invited address plus one new address is a normal case: the existing person is not inserted again, but they are still in guests, so they receive a second "you're scheduled" mail and a new calendar REQUEST, which can duplicate the event or reset RSVP. Only the filtered list should be treated as new guests.

findings.title: Seated bookings get bare Attendee rows with no seat check
findings.body: For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot, occupancy is tracked with BookingSeat rows tied to attendees. This update only createManys Attendee records. It never creates BookingSeat rows and never compares the result to seatsPerTimeSlot (that value is only copied onto the calendar payload at line 145). Seat counts and the attendee list diverge: availability that counts seats will ignore these people, while the bookings UI and the add-guest emails include them. seatsShowAttendees is not enforced before the full attendee list is emailed. Paid seated events can also gain people who never took or paid for a seat.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee. sendLocationChangeEmails just above, and the other senders in this file, return early when eventTypeDisableHostEmail or eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail is set (metadata.disableStandardEmails). The new function does not take event type metadata, and the handler loads the full eventType but does not pass it. Event types that turned standard emails off (workflows only, or privacy) still send booking details and ICS invites when a guest is added.

findings.title: Add guests is shown for past bookings
findings.body: The new additional_guests action is pushed into editBookingActions, which is nested in bookedActions. bookedActions is not only rendered for upcoming confirmed bookings; it is also rendered for past confirmed bookings (line 554) and past pending bookings (line 553). Those rows can open AddGuestsDialog and call addGuests. Combined with the handler not rejecting ended bookings, that sends confirmation mail and calendar updates for a meeting that already happened. The action should be limited to upcoming accepted bookings.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: The PR adds an authenticated mutation that writes attendees, updates calendars, and sends mail, and it adds no tests. There is no coverage for the admin/owner/organizer/attendee/stranger matrix, blacklist and case-insensitive dedup, booking status and disableGuests, seated events, or the branch that chooses AttendeeScheduledEmail versus AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The admin/owner condition is already wrong; a handler test with an admin who is not the host would have failed the merge.
